name: Terah
overview: Terah was a male figure in the early biblical narrative, identified as the son of Nahor. He is notably recognized as the father of Abram, Nahor, and Haran. His life is recorded in the Book of Genesis, where he is associated with the ancestral line leading to the nation of Israel.
namesAndTitles: The name Terah appears as a proper name in Genesis 11:24 without a given meaning or divine origin. No additional titles or meanings are recorded for this name in the biblical text.
familyAndRelationships: Terah is explicitly identified as the father of Abram, Nahor, Haran, and Sarai, establishing him as the patriarch of a significant family line. He is also noted as the son of another Nahor, linking him to a previous generation. These relationships are foundational to understanding his role in Scripture.
scriptureSignificance: Terah's significance lies in his position as the progenitor of Abram, through whom God would establish His covenant and bless all nations. His family's journey from Ur of the Chaldeans towards Canaan marks a pivotal transition from a pagan background to the unfolding of God's redemptive plan. Although Terah himself did not complete this journey, his lineage embodies the movement from idolatry to faith in the biblical narrative.

keyEvents.event: Became father of Abram, Nahor, and Haran
